description: Composite figure on low-density Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl (wt.%) TWIP steels, combining (a) a set of four mechanical-property plots with (b) a set of XRD-derived phase-fraction bar charts. All (a) panels share the x-axis "Al content / wt.%" (ticks 0, 2, 4, 5, 8, ~10.5; data points near 0, 2, 5, 8 and 10.5 wt.%) and four colour-coded conditions: as-quenched (black), 400 °C, 24h (blue), 500 °C, 24h (green), 600 °C, 24h (red). (a1) yield strength/MPa (y = 200–1200) is ~350 at 0 Al, dips near 2 Al, then rises steeply to the highest values (~690, 500 °C) at 10.5 Al; (a2) UTS/MPa (y = 500–1200) starts ~810–840, passes a minimum near 5 Al (~550–580) and climbs to ~900 (500 °C) at 10.5 Al; (a3) tensile elongation/% (y = 0–100) peaks at ~80–85% at 2 Al and collapses to ~12–25% at 10.5 Al; (a4) hardness/HBW (y = 100–600) has a minimum ~120–140 at 2 Al and reaches ~290 at 10.5 Al. Panel (b) plots phase fraction/vol.% (y = 0–100) versus tempering temperature/°C (0, 400, 500, 600), legend γ austenite (green), ε martensite (blue), α ferrite (red), κ carbide (magenta); one alloy (titled Fe-20Mn-0.4C-2Al) stays ~100% γ, while higher-Al alloys show increasing α ferrite and the highest-Al alloy develops κ carbide at 600 °C. The figure argues the Al-driven strength gain and ductility loss correlate mainly with ferrite content rather than ε martensite or κ carbide.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a 2x2 set of plots sharing the x-axis label 'Al content / wt.%'.
The four color-coded conditions are as-quenched (black), 400 °C, 24h (blue), 500 °C, 24h (green) and 600 °C, 24h (red).
In (a) yield strength reaches a minimum near 2 wt.% Al and rises steeply toward the maximum at the highest Al content (~10.5 wt.%).
In (a) tensile elongation peaks near 2 wt.% Al (touching the 80-90% region) and drops to roughly 10-25% at the highest Al content.
In (a) hardness passes a minimum near 2 wt.% Al (~120-140 HBW against the 100-200 gridlines) and rises to near the 300 HBW gridline at the highest Al content.
In (a) UTS is lowest for the as-quenched condition at 0 wt.% Al (black point ~640 MPa) whereas the three tempered series start at ~810-840 MPa.
Panel (b) legend assigns green = γ austenite, blue = ε martensite, red = α ferrite and magenta = κ carbide.
One phase-fraction chart is titled 'Fe-20Mn-0.4C-2Al' and shows essentially 100 vol.% γ austenite at every tempering temperature.
In the highest-Al phase-fraction chart the 600 °C bar contains a magenta κ carbide segment plus α ferrite (red) and γ austenite (green).
The legend of another phase-fraction chart includes ε martensite (blue), which appears only as a thin cap on top of the γ bars.
The caption states that (b) is the corresponding XRD analysis linking the observed strengthening and embrittlement phenomena to the constituting phases.
The citing text states that for Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl steels yield strength and UTS both increase while tensile elongation drops between 2 wt.% and 11 wt.% Al.
The citing text states that the increasing ferrite content seems more relevant to the property trend than the presence of κ carbides or ε-martensite.

subfigures.description: yield strength /MPa versus Al content / wt.%, y-axis 200-1200 MPa, four series (as-quenched, 400 °C 24h, 500 °C 24h, 600 °C 24h). Curve dips near 2 wt.% Al then rises steeply to highest values at ~10.5 wt.% Al.

UTS /MPa versus Al content / wt.%, y-axis 500-1200 MPa; as-quenched lowest at 0 Al (~640 MPa) while the three tempered series start ~810-840 MPa, pass a minimum near 5 wt.% Al and rise to ~900 MPa (500 °C) at ~10.5 wt.% Al.
tensile elongation /% versus Al content / wt.%, y-axis 0-100%. Peaks at ~80-85% near 2 wt.% Al, then falls monotonically to ~12-25% at ~10.5 wt.% Al; as-quenched is lowest at 0 Al (~28%).
hardness /HBW versus Al content / wt.%, y-axis 100-600 HBW. Minimum ~120-140 HBW near 2 wt.% Al, rising to ~290 HBW (500 °C) at ~10.5 wt.% Al.

Stacked bar charts of phase fraction /vol.% (y = 0-100) against tempering temperature /°C (0, 400, 500, 600) for successive Al-contents, legend γ austenite (green), ε martensite (blue), α ferrite (red), κ carbide (magenta). One chart (titled Fe-20Mn-0.4C-2Al) is ~100 vol.% γ; others contain α ferrite and, at 600 °C, κ carbide; bars in the first chart carry a small ε martensite cap.
